To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the streptococcic M-protein and streptolysine O can induce cellular autoimmunity in rabbits with respect to autogenous myocardial tissue.
the streptolysine and M-protein of group A streptococci induce cellular autoimmunity with respect to autogenic cardiac tissue in rabbits.
streptolysine O and M-protein are able to induce cellular immunity and autoimmune responses in rabbits with respect to autogenic cardiac tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an experimental model of cellular autoimmune disease of the heart.
the possibility of the existence of the immunopathogenic factors in the etiology of autoimmune diseases.
the problem of the role of streptococcus in the development of autoimmune processes in the organism and the mechanisms of the induction of anti-cardiac auto-immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the induction of cellular autoimmunity is a complex and multifactor process which includes the following stages: (a) modification of the antigenic properties of cardiac tissue; (b) modification of the immunological properties of lymphocyte system.
the experimental autoimmune response is induced by a complex interaction of various factors.

streptolysine O and M-protein, in the experimental conditions used, are capable of inducing both cellular and autoimmune responses with regard to autologous heart tissue, but that the latter are not due to a direct antigenic action of streptolysisin O or M protein, but rather to an alteration of cardiac tissue towards a "non-self" state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

streptolysins and M-protein are able to induce both cellular immunity and autoimmune reactions in the rabbit, and that this effect may be explained by the presence of the immunomorphological modifications in cardiac tissue and a shift in the functional balance of lymphocyte subpopulations.

both streptolysins and M-protein have a capacity to induce anti-cardiac cellular autoimmunity in genetically homogenous rabbits, and that this capacity is not related to their direct effect on the lymphocytes.
the induction of anti-cardiac auto- and cellular immune responses is possible only in the presence of a functional balance of the immunocompetent cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the induction of anti-cardiac auto-antibodies in rabbits is possible by means of the use of streptolysis and M-protein of group A streptococci, and that this process is accompanied by the induction of cellular autoimmunity.
streptococci can induce autoimmune reactions by the action of their pathogenic factors, which are able to change the immunomodulator status of cardiac tissue.
the induction of cellular immune responses in rabbits by streptolysis O and M-protein is associated with the appearance of anti-cardiac autoimmune response.
